standard_text: Amines: nomenclature, classification, structure, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, uses, identification of primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Diazonium salts: preparation, chemical reactions and importance in synthetic organic chemistry.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 9 Amines: classifying and naming amines, preparation, basic strength, tests for amines, diazonium salts and coupling reactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Amines are bases because of the lone pair on nitrogen.
key_sub: Aniline + HNO₂ at 273–278 K → diazonium salt.
body_html:
How to think about it

Amines are derivatives of ammonia, classed as 1°, 2° or 3° by the number of carbon groups on nitrogen. They are made by reducing nitro compounds, Gabriel synthesis and Hoffmann bromamide degradation. Alkylamines are stronger bases than ammonia; aniline is weaker because its lone pair is delocalised into the ring.

Primary amines give the carbylamine test; Hinsberg's reagent separates the three classes. Aniline forms benzenediazonium chloride at 273–278 K, which can be replaced by –Cl, –Br, –CN, –OH or –H, or coupled with phenol to give azo dyes.

Example

(CH₃)₂NH is?

two C on N

Answer: secondary amine

Example

Ethanamide + Br₂/NaOH?

one C fewer

Answer: methanamine

Common mistakes

  • Saying aniline is a stronger base than ammonia.
  • Giving the carbylamine test to secondary amines.
  • Calling an amide an amine.

faq.q: Why is aniline a weaker base than methanamine?
faq.a: Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, so it is less available to accept a proton.

faq.q: What is a diazonium salt used for?
faq.a: Making many aromatic compounds by replacing –N₂⁺, and making azo dyes by coupling.
